# Recall



* Slang is legit\! Bad words are legit\!
* Words get their meaning from history\, morphological processes\, and usage
* __Sociolinguistics __ is the study of the interaction of language and social factors
  * No one speaks the same way all the time\!
  * Social categories\, speech situation\, linguistic repertoire\, etc\.
  * Vary in all parts of the system
  * All languages change\!

---


# Regional variation

![](images/10-Who%20says%20pop%20and%20why_1.gif)



* __Regional variation __ has to do with how speakers in different parts of a country speak the same language differently
  * Differs from other kinds of variation \(e\.g\.\, age\, gender\, ethnicity\, community of practice\)
  * We’re talking about regional dialects\!

---


![](images/10-Who%20says%20pop%20and%20why_2.jpg)

# What’s a dialect?



* A  __dialect__  is the language variety characteristic of a particular regional\, ethnic\, or social group
  * It is systematically different from other varieties of the same language
  * Dialects of the same language are  __mutually intelligible__
  * It is different from an  __accent__
* Everyone has an accent\! Everyone has a dialect\!
* Dialects are not bad\! Dialects are just different\!
::: {.notes}

Dialect includes vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, pragmatics, and any other aspect of the linguistic system
Dialectology is the study of linguistic variation in dialects, often focused on mapping those differences; seek to understand what the differences are between varieties and why people continue to utilize these differences


:::

# To be able to talk about variation…



* We’re gonna need to go back to  __phonetics__ \!
  * The study of the sounds in a language
  * Two branches:  __Articulatory __ and  __acoustic__
* Our focus today is on articulatory\, which means we’re looking at the human vocal apparatus and how we configure it to make sounds\!

---




* A  __phonetic alphabet__  is a system of transcription which represents each speech sound with a single symbol and each symbol with a single speech sound\.
* Phonetic transcription is a one\-to\-one correspondence between sounds and symbols\.
* This eliminates the ambiguity of the sound\-symbol variations within a language or across languages\.
    * The most widely used phonetic alphabet is the  __International Phonetic Alphabet__
    * Why can’t we just use the English/Roman alphabet?\!

# Distinctive Features

![](images/10-Who%20says%20pop%20and%20why_9.jpg)



* For Consonants:
  * Voicing
  * Place of Articulation
  * Manner of Articulation
* For Vowels:
  * Tongue Height
  * Tongue Frontness
  * Tenseness
  * Lip Roundedness

---


# Describing Sounds: Consonants



* __Voicing:__  vibration of the vocal folds
  * If air is pushed between the vocal cords while they are held together\, they vibrate and create a  __voiced__  sound\.
  * If the vocal cords are held slightly apart\, air can flow through the space \(the glottis\) without causing a vibration\, thus creating a  __voiceless__  sound\.
* How can you tell?
  * Place your hand against your throat and say “sssssss” then “zzzzzzz”
  * If you feel buzzing\, it is voiced; if not\, it is voiceless


![](images/10-Who%20says%20pop%20and%20why_10.jpg)


---


# Q slide

True or false: \[s\] is voiced\, and \[z\] is voiceless\. \[False\]


---




* __Place of Articulation:__  Where the airstream is most obstructed
  * __Bilabial:__  two lips \[p\]\, \[b\]\, \[m\]
  * __Labiodental:__  lips and teeth \[f\]\, \[v\]
  * __Interdental:__  the ‘th’ sounds\, “thin\, then” \[θ\]\, \[ð\]
  * __Alveolar:__  tongue contacts the ridge behind the teeth \[t\]\, \[d\]\, \[s\]\, \[z\]\, \[n\]\, \[ɾ\]\, \[r\]\, \[l\]
  * __Alveopalatal:__  tongue makes contact between the alveolar ridge and the top of the palate\, “church\, judge” \[tʃ\]\, \[dʒ\]\, \[ʃ\]\, \[ʒ\]
  * __Palatal: __ tongue touches palate \[j\]
  * __Velar:__  Back of tongue contacts velum \[k\]\, \[g\]\, \[ŋ\]
    * __Labiovelar:__  velar with rounded lips \[w\]
  * __Glottal: __ sound made with glottis \[h\]\, \[ʔ\]


# Describing Sounds: Consonants


---




* __Manner of articulation:__  The particular way the airstream is obstructed
  * __Stops:__  air is built up in the vocal tract and suddenly released through the mouth
  * __Fricatives: __ continuous stream of air forced through a narrow opening
  * __Affricates: __ stop consonant released into a fricative; like a stop\-fricative combo
  * __Nasals: __ air redirected through nasal cavity instead of oral cavity
  * __Others: __ Liquids\, rhotics\, glides\, flaps\, trills\, clicks

---


# Describing (English) Vowels

![](images/10-Who%20says%20pop%20and%20why_11.jpg)

__Height:__  how high in your mouth is your tongue – high\, mid\, low

__Frontness__  __: __ how far forward in your mouth is your tongue – front\, central\, back

__Tenseness:__  the amount of muscle tension in the vocal tract – tense\, lax

__Roundedness:__  produced by rounding the lips – round\, unround


---


# Why are we talking about this?!



* To better understand what is meant by “people who sound different” \(= part of a dialect\)\, we have to have the right tools for discussion\!
  * Indeed\, many linguists believe that the sounds in a dialect are often not only the noticeable parts that vary but are also the place where we are seeing the most dynamic changes
  * And though many believe that the media is making us “all sound the same”\, research suggests that this is not the case
  * If anything\, constant contact with the world seems to be making people want to remember where they are from
